newsitem.title: UK: Moody's ups Qatar issuers sovereign ceilings.
newsitem.headline: Moody's ups Qatar issuers sovereign ceilings.

text.p: Moody's credit rating agency said on Monday it had upgraded the sovereign ceilings for ratings of long-term foreign currency-denominated bonds and bank deposits of issuers domiciled in Qatar to Baa2.
It also said the ceilings for ratings of foreign currency-denominated short-term obligations and deposits have been upgraded to Prime2.
Moody's said the upgrades were based on the country's improved economic and financial prospects, stemming primarily from the on-going development of its vast North Field gas reserves.
"With the recent completion on schedule of the first North Field gas project, Qatargas, the country is expected to begin exports of liquefied natural gas in January, 1997," Moody;s said.

"Receipts from from both Qatargas and the new Ras Laffan project are expected to reach $1.9 billion by the year 2001, and will provide the cashflow to service the associated large external debts raised by Qatar to finance its share of the projects."
Moody's said the construction phase of the Ras Laffan project will involve substantial external borrowing.

"However, Qatar is expanding its oil production capacity through the use of advanced technologies, and any additional foreign exchange receipts from a subsequent increase of crude oil exports could help to relieve financial pressures over this interim period," it said/
Moody's added that although Qatar's internal political situation appeared stable, as a small country in the midst of an unstable region, Qatar remained vulnerable to geopolitical risks.
